# Microsoft Entra Administrative Units — Adapter Technical Specification

![Entra Administrative Units adapter: OrgPath-facet-driven AU lifecycle, three-tier delegation model, and scoped role-assignment pipeline](images/entra-admin-units-image-01-au-adapter-architecture.png){#fig-entra-admin-units-image-01 fig-alt="Entra Administrative Units adapter architecture. Right column shows scoped role assignments in teal badges pinned to each tier: Global Reader / Security Reader at Tier 1, User Administrator / Groups Administrator at Tier 2, Helpdesk Administrator / Password Administrator at Tier 3. ## Canon-derived document

**Status:** `reserved` · **Class:** `modernization` · **Mission:** `integration` · **Phase:** `phase-planning`

**Canon source:** `UIAO_154_Delegation_Matrix_AUs_Roles.md` (v3.0, Model C) + ADR-037 (admin-unit-provisioning) + ADR-078 (15-facet schema).

This adapter provisions and governs the Entra Administrative Unit layer. It is the delegation-scope actuator in the UIAO Entra family, sitting alongside `entra-id` (identity fabric), `entra-dynamic-groups` (UIAO_152), `entra-id-governance` (PIM/lifecycle), and `entra-policy-targeting` (UIAO_164).
:::

## Overview

The **Entra Administrative Units Adapter** is the delegation-boundary actuator in the UIAO governance stack. It provisions, maintains, and audits Entra ID Administrative Units — the mechanism that replaces Active Directory's OU-based delegation model in a flat, cloud-native directory.

Active Directory delegated management authority implicitly through OU placement: assign a role on an OU, and it covered everything beneath it. Entra ID has no OU tree. The equivalent is an Administrative Unit with a membership rule and a scoped role assignment. The AU adapter makes that equivalence operational by:

1. **Deriving AUs from the OrgPath codebook** (UIAO_151). Every facet value or facet-tuple combination that appears in the delegation matrix (UIAO_154) corresponds to an AU definition that this adapter provisions and governs.
2. **Enforcing membership rule integrity**. AU membership rules are facet predicates (`extensionAttribute` expressions). The adapter validates them against the live codebook; a predicate referencing a retired facet value is a drift finding.
3. **Auditing role assignments**. Every scoped role assignment is recorded in the delegation matrix and verified against the live tenant. Unscoped assignments for AU-scopable roles are flagged as Governance Rule 4 violations.
4. **Enforcing the Restricted Management invariant**. All AUs in the governed estate must have `isMemberManagementRestricted: true`. The adapter detects and reports any AU without this flag.

**Implementation:** Planned for Phase 1 of the `entra-admin-units` track. Canon definition: UIAO_154 v3.0 (Model C). Provisioning ADR: ADR-037.

## What Administrative Units Replace

The table below maps the AD delegation patterns this adapter operationalizes to their Entra equivalents:

| Active Directory pattern | Entra ID equivalent (this adapter provisions) |
|---|---|
| Helpdesk rights on `OU=Baltimore` | `AU-Baltimore` with Authentication Administrator scoped |
| IT admin rights on `OU=East-Region` | `AU-US-East` with User Administrator scoped |
| Dept admin group management on `OU=Finance` | `AU-Department-Finance` with Groups Administrator scoped |
| Forest-level privileged admin | Global Administrator, PIM-eligible only (not provisioned by this adapter — see `entra-id-governance`) |
| Service account management OU | Service-account AU with Workload Identity Administrator scoped |
| Site-linked GPO scope | Not delegation — see `entra-policy-targeting` (Intune scope tags / CA named locations) |

## Three-Tier Delegation Model

Per UIAO_154 v3.0 (Model C), the delegation model organizes AUs into three tiers. The adapter provisions all tiers from the delegation matrix:

### Tier 1 — Enterprise AU

| AU Name | Membership Rule | Roles Scoped |
|---|---|---|
| `AU-Enterprise` | `(attr2 -ne "")` — any principal with a populated Department facet | Global Reader, Security Reader, Reports Reader |

The Enterprise AU is the "all governed users" scope. `isMemberManagementRestricted: true` is mandatory.

### Tier 2 — Department AUs

Membership rule: single `extensionAttribute2` predicate.

| AU Pattern | Example rule | Roles typically scoped |
|---|---|---|
| `AU-Department-IT` | `(attr2 -eq "IT")` | User Administrator, Groups Administrator |
| `AU-Department-Finance` | `(attr2 -eq "Finance")` | User Administrator, Groups Administrator |
| `AU-Department-HR` | `(attr2 -eq "HR")` | User Administrator |

One AU per active Department facet value in the codebook. The adapter creates a new Tier 2 AU when a new Department value is added to UIAO_151, and retires it (removing role assignments and then the AU) when the value is deprecated.

### Tier 3 — Division AUs

Membership rule: two-facet composition (`attr2` AND `attr3`).

| AU Pattern | Example rule | Roles typically scoped |
|---|---|---|
| `AU-IT-InfraOps` | `(attr2 -eq "IT") and (attr3 -eq "InfraOps")` | Helpdesk Administrator, Password Administrator |
| `AU-Finance-Payroll` | `(attr2 -eq "Finance") and (attr3 -eq "Payroll")` | Helpdesk Administrator |

### Cross-Cutting AUs

Membership rules composing facets from different dimensions — region × clearance, classification × department, etc.

```text
AU-Region-EASTUS-Privileged
  rule: (attr1 -eq "EASTUS") and (attr8 -eq "SECRET")
  roles: Authentication Administrator

AU-Classification-Contractor-All
  rule: (attr6 -eq "Contractor")
  roles: Helpdesk Administrator, Password Administrator

AU-IT-InfraOps-FullTime
  rule: (attr2 -eq "IT") and (attr3 -eq "InfraOps") and (attr6 -eq "Employee")
  roles: Groups Administrator
```

Cross-cutting AUs are declared explicitly in UIAO_154. The adapter does not infer them from the codebook — they require a delegation matrix entry.

## PIM + AU Interaction

AU scoping and PIM eligibility are independent layers that are always used together in the UIAO model:

| Layer | What it controls | How set |
|---|---|---|
| AU scope | Which objects a role covers (the *what*) | Membership rule on the AU |
| Role assignment | Which permission the role holder has (the *how*) | Scoped Entra role bound to the AU |
| PIM eligibility | Whether the permission is immediately active or requires elevation (the *when*) | All assignments in this adapter are **eligible**, never active |

::: {.callout-important}
**All role assignments provisioned by this adapter are PIM-eligible, not permanently active.** A permanently active role assignment within the governed AU estate is a drift finding regardless of scope.
:::

PIM activation requirements per role tier (configured in `entra-id-governance`):

| Role tier | Justification required | Approval required | Max session |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 (Global Reader) | No | No | 8 hours |
| Tier 2 (User Administrator) | Yes | No | 4 hours |
| Tier 3 (Helpdesk Administrator) | Yes (RITM number) | No | 4 hours |
| Elevated (Authentication Admin) | Yes | Supervisor approval | 2 hours |
| Privileged (Privileged Role Admin) | Yes | Dual approval | 1 hour |

## Scope

**Reads:** Microsoft Graph AU endpoints (`/directory/administrativeUnits`, `/directory/administrativeUnits/{id}/members`, `/directory/administrativeUnits/{id}/scopedRoleMembers`).

**Writes:** Creates, updates, and retires AUs per UIAO_154. Modifies membership rules and role assignments. All writes are idempotent and logged.

**Does NOT:** Modify user objects or group objects. Does not activate PIM sessions (that is `entra-id-governance`). Does not assign licenses or conditional access policies.

## Canon Invariants

Per ADR-037 and UIAO_154 Governance Rule 4:

1. Every AU in the governed estate has `isMemberManagementRestricted: true`.
2. Every AU membership rule references only active facet values from UIAO_151.
3. Every role that has an AU-scope option is scoped to an AU — not assigned tenant-wide.
4. Every role assignment is PIM-eligible, not permanently active.
5. Cross-cutting AUs have an explicit entry in UIAO_154 — they are not inferred.

Violations of any invariant are surfaced as drift findings by the adapter's audit run.

## Controls

| Control | Role | Capability |
|---|---|---|
| **AC-2** Account Management | Primary | AU scope ensures administrative access tracks org structure automatically |
| **AC-5** Separation of Duties | Primary | Tier-scoped roles prevent any single administrator from having tenant-wide authority |
| **AC-6** Least Privilege | Primary | AU scope + PIM eligibility enforces minimum necessary access |
| **AC-6(2)** Non-Privileged Access | Supporting | Governance Rule 4 blocks unscoped role assignments |
| **AU-2** Audit Events | Supporting | Every role activation (PIM) and AU membership change is logged |
